summary: Reviewed server.js/store.js. Tests pass, but a probe shows any authenticated user can read another user's note (IDOR) and errors leak stack traces.

criteria.description: Users can only access their own notes
Core CRUD works and tests pass

findings.title: IDOR: GET /notes/:id lacks owner check
findings.detail: src/server.js GET-by-id returns store.get(id) without comparing note.owner to X-User. Probe: mallory read alice's note with 200 (ev:ev-muzjj2nv-0164a6a4). DELETE does check ownership; GET does not.
findings.recommendation: Return 404 when note.owner !== user, same as DELETE; add a cross-user test for GET and DELETE.

findings.title: Error responses leak stack traces; malformed JSON gives 500
findings.detail: catch block returns err.stack in the 500 body. Invalid JSON POST returned 500 with a SyntaxError message (ev:ev-muzjj2nv-0164a6a4). Exposes internal paths.
findings.recommendation: Return 400 for parse/validation errors, and a generic 500 message while logging the stack server-side. Validate title/body types.

findings.title: No body size limit or auth beyond a spoofable X-User header
findings.detail: readBody is unbounded, and X-User is trusted as identity. Not demonstrated as in scope for this phase.
findings.recommendation: Cap body size (e.g. 1MB); document X-User as a placeholder until real authn.
